records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Well, I told you John T. Golle. He was working with Roundup Monsanto on their launch. So I guess him and Jerri (Jerri Frantzve), Jerri (Jerri Frantzve)'s with DuPont. That's a natural alliance poisoning the population and getting away with it.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Current corporate and biographical searches did not locate reliable evidence that John T. Golle worked for Monsanto to launch Roundup.

records.text: On February 26, Trump signed an executive order invoking the Defense Production Act to boost glyphosate production.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Because on February 26th, Trump signed an executive order invoking the Defense Production Act to boost the production of glyphosate, which is what's found in Monsanto, right?

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 39:38. The White House and Federal Register establish that Executive Order 14387 was signed February 18, 2026, not February 26. The rest is substantially accurate: it invoked Defense Production Act authority for elemental phosphorus and glyphosate-based herbicides.

sources.title: Promoting the National Defense by Ensuring an Adequate Supply of Elemental Phosphorus and Glyphosate-Based Herbicides - White House
sources.relevance: Primary order confirms the Defense Production Act action and shows it was signed February 18, not February 26.

records.text: Glyphosate is a cancer-causing agent in weed killer.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That is the cancer-causing agent that is in the weed killer. We know it causes cancer. MAHA mom spot.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 39:51. IARC classifies glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans based on limited human and sufficient animal evidence, while EPA's current position is that it is unlikely to be a human carcinogen and presents no human-health risk of concern when label directions are followed. The categorical 'we know it causes cancer' overstates a disputed assessment.

sources.title: IARC Monographs evaluation of glyphosate
sources.relevance: IARC classifies glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans.

sources.title: Glyphosate - U.S. EPA
sources.relevance: EPA says glyphosate is unlikely to be a human carcinogen and finds no human-health risks when used according to label, explaining the mixed rating.
